headline: CHALICE MAKES HIGH-GRADE TENNANT CREEK DISCOVERY: 15M @ 8.6 G/T GOLD, 0.54% COPPER — 2M @ 56.7 G/T INSIDE, 500M STRIKE OPEN
snippet: Chalice Mining (ASX: CHN) announced November 2 that first-ever drilling at its Kestrel prospect, Warrego North project in the Northern Territory's Tennant Creek Mineral Field, hit high-grade gold-copper mineralization: discovery hole WCRC001 returned 15m at 8.6 g/t gold and 0.54% copper from 78m depth, including a 2m high-grade core at 56.7 g/t gold, with follow-up holes confirming 27m at 0.57% copper and 24m at 0.52% copper. The strike extent is at least 500m and open in all directions, with a ~2.2km magnetic anomaly still undrilled; the geology is consistent with iron oxide copper-gold (IOCG) mineralization — the same style that produced the historic Warrego mine (~1.3 Moz gold, ~91kt copper) immediately nearby, making this one of the most significant exploration announcements out of Australia so far in November.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES 0.8% TO $3,904, SILVER SURGES 2.5% TO $50 — OIL'S 3%+ DROP ON IRAN-DOHA TALKS FUELS MONDAY METALS RECOVERY
snippet: Spot gold recovered to approximately US$3,904/oz on Monday November 2 — up ~0.8% after touching a one-year low on Friday — and silver rebounded to ~US$50/oz (up ~2.5%), as oil prices fell more than 3% when Reuters reported Iranian negotiators were in Doha for indirect peace talks with Qatari mediators, easing inflation fears and reducing Fed rate-hike urgency. Gold had dropped 3.5% on Friday; analysts caution that three Fed officials reiterated hawkish guidance on Friday (further hikes possible) and the 50-day SMA near US$3,978 remains the key ceiling — a close above it would signal October's correction is complete, while failure leaves the $3,500–3,750 Fibonacci zone as the next structural floor.

headline: AMERICAN LITHIUM MACUSANI URANIUM RESOURCE HITS ~57M LB U₃O₈ — $100/LB PRICE BASIS ADOPTED; PERU SPIN-OUT ADVANCES
snippet: American Lithium Corp. (TSX: LI) released an updated Mineral Resource estimate for its Macusani uranium project in Peru on November 2, shifting to a US$100/lb uranium price assumption (up from US$50/lb previously) and upgrading a larger proportion of the resource to Measured and Indicated categories, with total M&I now approximately 57 million lb U₃O₈ (effective date July 1, 2026). The company is actively advancing plans to spin out the Macusani uranium assets as a separate entity, a move intended to unlock value at a time when spot uranium holds near US$90/lb; for investors tracking Western Hemisphere uranium supply chains, Macusani is one of the largest undeveloped uranium deposits outside of Kazakhstan and Australia, giving the planned spin-out vehicle a credible foundation.

headline: PHOENIX COPPER EMPIRE MINE RESERVE SURGES 31.5% TO 13.27MT — IDAHO OPEN-PIT COPPER PROJECT HEADS FOR UPDATED PFS
snippet: Phoenix Copper (AIM: PXC) published an updated Mineral Reserve Statement for its Empire Open-Pit Mine in Idaho, showing 13.27 million tonnes of proven and probable reserves — a 31.49% increase in tonnage and a 26.31% increase in copper equivalent metal versus the May 2024 estimate, prepared by Hardrock Consulting. An updated Pre-Feasibility Study incorporating the expanded reserve is targeted for completion before year-end; the company also raised $3.12 million in equity and believes higher copper prices (LME copper averaged ~US$6.40/lb in Q3 2026) materially improve project economics — a significant reserve expansion milestone for a US-hosted copper project at a time Western copper supply chain development is a policy priority.

headline: SINDA (TSXV: SDA) DRILLS 31,150 METRES WITH 18 RIGS AT CARACOL SILVER-GOLD IN Q3 — EXPLORATION DECLINE ON TRACK
snippet: Sinda Ltd. (TSXV: SDA) reported Q3 2026 results on November 2 showing 18 drill rigs turned approximately 31,150 metres at its Caracol silver-gold project in Mexico during the quarter — intensive surface drilling while simultaneously advancing an exploration decline that will enable underground diamond drilling from within the deposit. Assay results are being released on a rolling basis as they are received and confirmed; the exploration decline, which is nearing completion, is the key catalyst for Caracol's geological model resolution and a potential NI 43-101 resource estimate, positioning this high-drill-activity Mexico silver-gold story among the better-resourced exploration campaigns on the TSX-V right now.

headline: GLOBAL LITHIUM COMMENCES MANNA EARLY WORKS IN WA — CONSTRUCTION PREP SIGNALS CONVICTION DESPITE PRICE WEAKNESS
snippet: Global Lithium Resources (ASX: GL1) has commenced early works at its Manna lithium project in Western Australia's Eastern Goldfields, beginning site infrastructure and contractor mobilization activities even as Chinese lithium carbonate futures sit near 88,500 yuan/tonne — a fraction of the 2022 peak. The decision to proceed with early works during a lithium price trough signals management's conviction in the project timeline and a long-term view that battery metal demand will recover; for retail investors tracking lithium developers, Manna is among the larger hard-rock spodumene projects advancing toward construction in WA, and the early works commencement begins the clock on construction milestones that will matter when the market eventually turns.

headline: BARGAIN HUNTERS RETURN TO GOLD AND SILVER AFTER WORST OCTOBER SINCE 2008 — CAN GOLD RECLAIM $3,978 WITH FED HAWKS STILL CIRCLING?
snippet: A November 2 FXEmpire analysis frames gold's 7.4% October decline — its worst monthly loss since 2008 — as having finally attracted value buyers, with the critical technical test being the 50-day SMA near US$3,978; a weekly close above it would signal the correction is complete and open the door to a retest of the $4,200 zone, while failure to hold Monday's bounce would accelerate selling toward the Fibonacci support at US$3,500–3,750. The piece identifies the three hawks (Fed officials who reiterated rate hike openness on Friday, November 1) as the ceiling on any recovery, and notes that the gold-silver ratio's recent extreme above 79 — now pulling back — has historically preceded outsized silver recoveries once the macro catalyst arrives.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' SEASONALLY STRONGEST MONTH HAS ARRIVED — HUI MINERS AVERAGE 4%+ IN NOVEMBER ACROSS BULL MARKET YEARS
snippet: A GoldSeek seasonal analysis argues that November marks the beginning of gold stocks' strongest historical stretch, with the NYSE Arca Gold BUGS Index (HUI) averaging approximately 4.1% in November and roughly 19.9% across the full November–February window during modern gold bull market years — nearly double gold's own seasonal average gain over the same period. The analysis arrives at a moment of extreme negative sentiment after October's equity selloff, citing the historical pattern of that combination (deep October correction + bearish capitulation + entering the November seasonal window) as the setup that has produced the sharpest multi-month recoveries in prior cycles, including 2015–2016 and 2018; for junior gold miners already at multi-year relative lows, the seasonal thesis supports accumulation in the current window even as near-term macro risks remain unresolved.

headline: BMO COMPLETES EUROZ HARTLEYS MINING CAPITAL MARKETS BUY — STRONGER PERTH-BASED COVERAGE FOR ASX JUNIOR MINERS
snippet: BMO Financial Group completed its acquisition of the Australian capital markets business of Euroz Hartleys Group Limited on November 1, 2026, adding Perth-based metals and mining advisory, research, and equities execution capabilities to BMO Capital Markets' global mining franchise. The deal expands institutional research coverage of ASX-listed junior and mid-tier miners at a time when Australian resource companies are navigating post-October equity weakness; for junior mining companies, stronger institutional coverage from a bank with deep global mining credentials is a meaningful improvement in access to capital and investor visibility — particularly relevant as the November–February seasonal window historically favors sector re-rating.
